'''''Begonia'' × ''hiemalis''''', the '''elatior begonia''' or '''Reiger begonia''', is an artificial hybrid species of flowering plant in the family [[Begoniaceae]].<ref name="ABS_xch" >{{cite web |url=https://www.begonias.org/hiemalis-reiger-elatior-xcheimantha |title=Hiemalis, Reiger, Elatior, & ×Cheimantha |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2024 |website=begonias.org |publisher=American Begonia Society |access-date=31 May 2024 }}</ref> Its parents are ''[[Begonia socotrana]]'' and ''[[Begonia × tuberhybrida]]'' (itself a hybrid of multiple species).<ref name="POWO_104845-1" >{{cite POWO |id=104845-1 |title=''Begonia'' × ''hiemalis'' Fotsch |access-date=31 May 2024 }}</ref> Hybridization efforts began in 1881, with the first cultivar named 'John Heal'.<ref name="ABS_xch" /> The 'Elatior' cultivar debuted in 1906, and beginning in 1950 Otto Rieger issued many new, disease-resistant cultivars, such that people began to call the group "elatior" or "Rieger" begonias.<ref name="ABS_xch" /> In addition to their typically [[Double-flowered|doubled flowers]] which come in every color except blue, they are valued for their tendency to bloom in fall and winter, and in fact nearly year-round.<ref name="ABS_xch" />
